questions.prompt: Your property sits next to a Maui County street. You usually must keep the sidewalk or shoulder free of weeds. Which owners are left out of this duty?
choices: Owners of lots bigger than 15 acres in agricultural districts
People who rent instead of own
Owners of oceanfront lots
Anyone whose lot is smaller than one acre
questions.answer: Owners of lots bigger than 15 acres in agricultural districts
questions.excerpt:
Unless otherwise expressly stated, whenever used in this chapter the following terms
               shall be taken to have the following meanings: "Owner" means the fee simple owner, lessee of record, administrator, administratrix,
               executor, executrix, receiver, trustee, property management agent, or any other individual,
               corporation, partnership, or association who has control or possession of privately
               owned real property; provided, however, that this term shall not include the owners
               of real property within agricultural districts whose lots exceed fifteen acres. "Sidewalk" means that portion of a street between a curbline or the pavement of a
               road, and the adjacent property line, including any setback area acquired by the county
               for road-widening purposes. "Weeds" means vegetation of such nature, which has reached such growth, and is present
               in such quantity, that it constitutes a substantial risk of one or more of the following
               hazards: 1. The vegetation, when dry, is or will be a fire hazard; 2. The vegetation is, or is naturally suited as sheltering or breeding place for rats,
                  mice, mosquitoes, or other vermin or noxious insects; or 3. The vegetation overgrows or spreads upon or over any road, alley, path, or sidewalk
                  owned or open to the public, to such extent as to obstruct, impede, or interfere with
                  the safe or convenient use or maintenance thereof. (Ord. 3493 § 1, 2007: Ord. 1392 § 1 (part), 1984)

Every property owner whose land abuts or adjoins a County street shall continually
               maintain, and keep clean, passable and free from weeds and noxious growths, the sidewalk
               or shoulder areas which abut or adjoin the owner's property. (Ord. 3493 § 2, 2007: Ord. 1392 § 1 (part), 1984)

questions.prompt: When can overgrown plants be treated as "weeds" under these sidewalk rules?
choices: When they are a fire hazard when dry, a hiding place for rats, mice or mosquitoes, or they block a public road or sidewalk
Whenever they grow taller than the curb
Only if a neighbor complains about how they look
Only if they are plants that are not native to Hawaii
questions.answer: When they are a fire hazard when dry, a hiding place for rats, mice or mosquitoes, or they block a public road or sidewalk

choices: 20 days
7 days
30 days
48 hours

questions.prompt: How must the County send the official notice to clean the sidewalk?
choices: By certified mail to the owner's last known address
By regular first-class mail
By hanging a tag on the mailbox
By posting a sign on the sidewalk
questions.answer: By certified mail to the owner's last known address

questions.prompt: To dig up a County street or sidewalk you generally need a written permit from the department of public works and waste management plus 8 hours' notice to police. What work may start without that permit and notice?
choices: Emergency repairs of sewer lines or water mains
Planting street trees
Fixing a pothole in front of your house
Installing a new driveway
questions.answer: Emergency repairs of sewer lines or water mains
